definition: Serendipity means a fortunate discovery made by accident.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word serendipity. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know serendipity should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Half the apps on your phone began, their founders admit, in serendipity - a bug, a wrong file, a demo that failed in an interesting way.
Coincidence is two things merely happening together, with nothing gained; serendipity hands you a discovery.
Luck favors you in general - a green light, a good seat; serendipity is more particular, an accident that delivers a delightful find.

Happenstance is neutral chance — things simply falling out one way rather than another, lucky or not. Serendipity is never neutral: the accident must hand you a fortunate discovery, something valuable you were not seeking. Happenstance describes the roll; serendipity describes what the roll delivered.

A windfall is an unexpected gain, usually money, that simply drops on you — a rebate, an inheritance, fruit off a neighbor's tree. Serendipity turns on a discovery: the accident shows you something, and an alert mind must notice it. A windfall needs no noticing at all.

A fluke is an improbable success at the very thing you were attempting — the mishit shot that somehow drops in. Serendipity delivers what you were not attempting at all: an accident hands you a valuable find off to the side of your search.
an outcome produced on purpose, by plan
chance working against you

There is no root to reuse - Serendip is simply the old name for Sri Lanka. Horace Walpole invented serendipity in 1754 after the tale of the island's three princes, forever finding treasures they were not seeking. Every later use of the word retells their story in miniature.
Serendipity means a fortunate discovery made by accident.

Looking for her dropped earring under the theater seats, Amaya's flashlight caught a corner of paper taped beneath row F: a signed playbill from the opening night of 1962, exactly what the anniversary exhibit lacked.
The earring stayed lost; the museum called it serendipity.
Serendipity is not plain luck: luck merely favors you, and coincidence merely happens.
Serendipity requires a find - something valuable you were not looking for, delivered by accident to someone alert enough to notice it.
Lose an earring, find an archive.
Serendipity is friendly and story-shaped; science writing and travel essays love it.
Use luck for general good fortune; save serendipity for the moment an accident hands you a discovery - the word itself implies that something was found.

The graduate student was in the basement stacks to settle a dull question: which year the county courthouse had replaced its roof.
The insurance ledger she needed had been shelved, decades ago, inside a box of unrelated papers — and beneath it lay a bundle of letters tied in string, addressed in a hand she almost recognized.
They were the town founder's letters home, presumed burned since the 1930s.
Historians had written whole arguments around their absence.
She later called the find serendipity and meant it precisely: she had not been looking for letters, would never have looked in that box, and nearly put the bundle back unopened.
The roof, her notes record, was replaced in 1911.
Nobody has ever cited that fact.
